title: What Really Drives Gas Prices? The Data Behind the Pump

segments.label: scene 1 (title)
segments.text: Every driver knows the sinking feeling at the pump when prices suddenly surge. In June 2022, regular gas hit an all-time peak of $4.93 per gallon.

segments.label: scene 2 (gauge)
segments.text: Even after pulling back, fuel costs are climbing fast again. By November 2026, the national average stood at $4.15 per gallon.

segments.label: scene 3 (heatmap)
segments.text: Over the last year alone, from November 2025 to November 2026, gas prices jumped by 36.2%.

segments.label: scene 4 (multiline)
segments.text: During that same twelve-month period, crude oil surged by 66.2%, reaching $100 per barrel in November 2026.

segments.label: scene 5 (bars)
segments.text: That far outpaces overall inflation, with consumer prices rising just 3.7% over the year ending in September 2026.

segments.label: scene 6 (statement)
segments.text: Gas prices clearly rise faster and drop sharper than everyday goods. So what causes these relentless swings at the pump?

segments.label: scene 7 (kpi)
segments.text: To unpack what drives fuel costs, we must follow the journey from raw crude to the retail pump.

segments.label: scene 8 (line)
segments.text: To understand where fuel costs are heading, we have to look back across three decades of data, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

segments.label: scene 9 (compare)
segments.text: Back in August 1990, regular gasoline averaged just $1.22 per gallon for American drivers at the pump.

segments.label: scene 10 (counter)
segments.text: Prices dropped even lower by the end of that decade, reaching an absolute historic floor of $0.92 per gallon in February 1999.

segments.label: scene 11 (heatmap)
segments.text: That bargain floor quickly dissolved into decades of heavy volatility, as shifting global market forces repeatedly drove fuel prices higher.

segments.label: scene 12 (counter)
segments.text: Spikes grew dramatically sharper over time, including an earlier major peak in July 2008 when regular gas reached $4.06.

segments.label: scene 13 (multiline)
segments.text: Over the long run, consumer prices increased +164% since January 1990, showing how fuel outpaced everyday household inflation.

segments.label: scene 14 (statement)
segments.text: From August 1990 to November 2026, regular gas climbed +241%, standing at 3.4 times its initial baseline.

segments.label: scene 15 (statement)
segments.text: Every pump shock starts upstream in global energy trading. Geopolitical disruptions and supply cuts send raw oil prices climbing fast.

segments.label: scene 16 (line)
segments.text: In June 2008, crude oil rocketed to its highest recorded peak of $134 per barrel.

segments.label: scene 17 (counter)
segments.text: By April 2011, another price shock pushed crude back up to $109 per barrel. That was a +30% increase in a single year.

segments.label: scene 18 (multiline)
segments.text: Global supply constraints struck again in June 2022 as crude reached $115 per barrel. Upstream crude prices surged +61% over the preceding year.

segments.label: scene 19 (counter)
segments.text: At retail stations, gas surged to $4.48 per gallon in May 2026. That represented a +42% jump over twelve months.

segments.label: scene 20 (bars)
segments.text: Looking back across two decades, since January 2005 crude oil has climbed +113%, while regular gas prices have increased +127%.

segments.label: scene 21 (compare)
segments.text: Consider how wild that swing is compared to December 1998, when crude hit a rock-bottom $11 per barrel. Violent boom-and-bust cycles constantly reframe retail fuel costs.

segments.label: scene 22 (statement)
segments.text: Crude oil is the single primary factor shaping retail gas prices. When global crude benchmarks shift, station prices follow almost immediately.

segments.label: scene 23 (counter)
segments.text: To understand market dynamics, look at early baseline pricing. In January 1990, West Texas Intermediate crude traded at $23 per barrel.

segments.label: scene 24 (line)
segments.text: As global energy demand expanded, benchmark prices trended higher. Crude oil increased +337% from January 1990 to November 2026.

segments.label: scene 25 (counter)
segments.text: Despite wild swings over three decades, baseline pricing moved upward. By November 2026, crude oil reached $100 per barrel.

segments.label: scene 26 (compare)
segments.text: Global market dynamics regularly reset energy price baselines. Benchmark crude climbed from $58 in January 2020 to $76 in January 2025.

segments.label: scene 27 (bars)
segments.text: Refinery shifts and crude movements created long-term divergence. Since January 2010, crude oil increased +27%, while regular gas surged +53%.

segments.label: scene 28 (statement)
segments.text: Upstream oil trading establishes the underlying cost for every gallon. Global crude market dynamics ultimately drive ongoing pump volatility.

segments.label: scene 29 (statement)
segments.text: While standard household goods follow a steady upward path over time, retail energy costs swing with far sharper velocity.

segments.label: scene 30 (line)
segments.text: Across the entire broader economy, overall consumer prices stand 2.6 times higher today than they did back in January 1990.

segments.label: scene 31 (line)
segments.text: Comparing long-term trends, since January 2000 general consumer inflation rose +99%, while regular gas prices surged +222%.

segments.label: scene 32 (kpi)
segments.text: Focusing on recent history, since January 2015 broad consumer prices increased +43%, whereas retail fuel jumped +96%.

segments.label: scene 33 (multiline)
segments.text: Upstream crude oil moved even faster over that exact stretch, advancing +108% since January 2015.

segments.label: scene 34 (kpi)
segments.text: Even during the nationwide inflation shock of June 2022, general consumer prices increased by just +9% over twelve months.

segments.label: scene 35 (counter)
segments.text: At its peak in June 2022, regular gasoline reached an all-time high of $4.93 per gallon.

segments.label: scene 36 (line)
segments.text: Crude oil reached its all-time peak of $134 in June 2008, kicking off years of dramatic market swings.

segments.label: scene 37 (statement)
segments.text: Pump prices do not move alongside typical household goods. They track the global crude market through every sudden geopolitical and supply shock.

segments.label: scene 38 (counter)
segments.text: Recent market shifts highlight how rapidly retail fuel reacts. From January 2025 to November 2026, regular gas moved up +35%.

segments.label: scene 39 (slope)
segments.text: Over that exact span, crude oil climbed +32%. The direct connection between crude benchmark trading and your local pump stays unbroken.

segments.label: scene 40 (kpi)
segments.text: When upstream crude moves, retail stations adjust fast. Ultimately, gas prices reflect global energy commodity markets rather than standard inflation trends.

segments.label: scene 41 (gauge)
segments.text: With regular gas at $4.15 a gallon, do you expect prices to trend higher or lower over the next year? Tell us in the comments.

segments.label: scene 42 (statement)
segments.text: Subscribe to Plotline Data for more data stories explaining the numbers shaping your world. Which of these numbers surprised you most? Tell us in the comments.
